e3cf4d.conditions: none; every wildcard exchange is a single round (at most one message per sender-receiver pair) bracketed by barriers or a completed handshake
e3cf4d.reasoning: The four point_values calls reuse the same tag (remote_point_evaluation) and probe with MPI_ANY_SOURCE (mpi_remote_point_evaluation.h:901). Without fencing, a fast rank's next-round message could be taken in place of a slow rank's current one. But evaluate_and_process takes a static CollectiveMutex, whose lock and unlock both call a blocking MPI_Barrier (mpi.cc:1993/2037), so the rounds cannot overlap. Within one round each sender sends exactly one message to each receiver, and the receiver places it by status.MPI_SOURCE, so arrival order does not matter. During setup, PEX (used for 4 ranks) is also wrapped in a CollectiveMutex. It counts sources with the request/answer NBX: a rank enters Ibarrier only after its targets have answered, so every request has been consumed before the barrier completes. Each wildcard probe there gets at most one message per source and uses a distinct tag. All sends are nonblocking Isends, so no deadlock depends on buffering.
